title: Martial arts programs that train people to sense being looked at
summary: Rupert Sheldrake tells of Martial arts programs that train people to sense being looked at, about an unknown time at an unknown place, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: because in the martial arts there are various martial arts programs where they train people to know when they're being looked at from behind

plain: Rupert Sheldrake, a biologist known for unusual ideas about the mind, told podcast host Jesse Michels in 2024 that some martial arts programmes train people to know when they are being looked at from behind. He offers this as support for his view that people really can sense being stared at, which would mean attention reaches beyond the body.
